By (loc. cit.) the canonical arrows \[ K^+(\overline{u}'^*)(F') \longrightarrow r_1^*(J') \quad \text{and} \quad K^+(\overline{u}^*)(F') \longrightarrow r_o^*(J') \] are quasi-isomorphisms (cf. (1.2.8) for the notations). We consequently obtain a morphism \[ \mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}'_* \circ \mathrm{L}^+\overline{u}'^*(F') \xrightarrow{\ \eta^f(F')\ } \mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}_* \circ \mathrm{L}^+\overline{u}^*(F') \] such that the following diagram commutes in \(\mathrm{D}^+(S)\): \[ (3.1.1.8) \qquad \xymatrix@!0@C=11em@R=5.5em{ & Q \circ K^+(\overline{u}'_*)(r_o^*(J')) \ar[rr]^-{\sim} \ar[dd] & & \mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}'_* \circ Q(r_o^*(J')) \ar[dd] \\ Q \circ K^+(\overline{u}'_*) \circ K^+(\overline{u}'^*)(F') \ar[ur] \ar[rr]^(0.56){\sim} \ar[dd]_{Q(K^+(\alpha_f)(F'))} & & \mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}'_* \circ \mathrm{L}^+\overline{u}'^*(F') \ar[ur] \ar[dd]^(0.36){\eta^f(F')} & \\ & Q \circ K^+(\overline{u}_*)(r_1^*(J')) \ar[rr]^(0.62){\sim} & & \mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}_* \circ Q(r_1^*(J')) \\ Q \circ K^+(\overline{u}_*) \circ K^+(\overline{u}^*)(F') \ar[ur] \ar[rr] & & \mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}_* \circ \mathrm{L}^+\overline{u}^*(F') \ar[ur] & } \]
It is clear that \(\eta^f(F')\) does not depend on the chosen resolution, and one verifies that it is functorial in \(F'\) varying in \(\mathrm{D}^+(S)\).
To complete the proof of (3.1.1), it suffices to prove the following lemma:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (3.1.1.9)

Let \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\) and \(X' \xrightarrow{\ u'\ } C_S^\Delta\) be two objects of \(\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{plat}}(\Delta^{o}, B/S)\). Let \(f, g : X \longrightarrow X'\) be two morphisms in \(\mathrm{Hom}(\Delta^{o}, B/S)\): if there exists a simplicial homotopy from \(f\) to \(g\), then \(\eta^f = \eta^g\).

Let \(h_n : \mathrm{Hom}_\Delta([n], [1]) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Hom}_{B/S}(X_n, X'_n)\) be a simplicial homotopy from \(f\) to \(g\). Let \(\overline{I \times D}\) be the category obtained from \(I \times D\) by adjoining the arrows \((1, n) \to (0, n)\) corresponding bijectively to \(h_n\,(\mathrm{Hom}([n], [1]))\) and the relations imposed by the compatibility of the \(h_n\) for varying \(n\). The data of the lemma define a flat augmentation \([X\,|_f\,X'] \xrightarrow{\ t\ } C_S^{\overline{I \times D}}\). Let \(F'\) be a complex of \(C^+(S)\) and \(J'\) a resolution of \(C^+(\overline{e}^*)(F')\) such that for every integer \(n\), \(J^n\) is totally acyclic object by object: there exists a simplicial homotopy between \[ C^+(\underline{\Gamma}(u'_*))(r_o^*(J')) \rightrightarrows C^+(\underline{\Gamma}(u_*))(r_1^*(J')) \] whence a homotopy on passing to the "condensed" complexes. (cf. (3.0.2.3)).

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.html:
Definition (3.1.2)

With the notations of (3.1.1), we shall say that \(f\) is an equivalence for \(G\)-1-cohomological descent if \(\eta_G^f\) is an isomorphism.

(3.1.3) In what follows we shall denote by \(L_i : \Delta \to \Delta \times \Delta\) (resp. \(c_i : \Delta \to \Delta \times \Delta\)) the canonical functor defined by \([n] \to [n] \times [i]\) (resp. \([n] \to [i] \times [n]\)).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (3.1.4)

Let \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^{\Delta \times \Delta}\) and \(X' \xrightarrow{\ u'\ } C_S^{\Delta \times \Delta}\) be two objects of \(\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{plat}}((\Delta \times \Delta)^{o}, B/S)\). Let \(f : X \longrightarrow X'\) be a morphism over \(S\): suppose that \(f * \mathrm{id}_{L_i} : X \circ L_i \to X' \circ L_i\) (resp. \(f * \mathrm{id}_{c_i} : X \circ c_i \to X' \circ c_i\)) is an equivalence for \(G\)-1-cohomological descent for every integer \(i\). Then \(f\) is an equivalence for \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.

By the description of \(\eta^f\) (cf. proof of (3.1.1)) it is a matter of showing that a certain morphism of triple complexes induces an isomorphism on the cohomology of the condensed complexes: a standard spectral sequence argument then allows us to conclude.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (3.1.5)

Let \(X\) and \(X'\) be two objects of \(\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{plat}}(\Delta^{o}, B/S)\). Let \(f : X \longrightarrow X'\) be a functorial morphism such that \(f_n : X_n \longrightarrow X'_n\) is a morphism of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent. Then the canonical morphism \([[X\,|_f\,X']] \longrightarrow [[X'\,|_{\mathrm{id}}\,X']]\) (cf. (1.2.7)) is an equivalence for \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.
This follows from (3.1.4) and the following lemma, whose proof is left to the reader:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (3.1.5.1)

Let \(f : R \longrightarrow S\) be a flat morphism, and let \(Y \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\) and \(Y \xrightarrow{\ v\ } C_R^\Delta\) be two flat augmentations such that the following diagram commutes in \(\mathrm{Hom}(\Delta^{o}, B)\): \[ \xymatrix@R=2em@C=2em{ Y \ar[rr]^-{v} \ar[dr]_-{u} & & C_R^\Delta \ar[dl]^-{f} \\ & C_S^\Delta & } \] If \(v\) is an augmentation of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent, then it is an equivalence for \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.
In the applications, we shall combine (3.1.4) and (3.1.5) with the following result:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (3.1.6)

Let \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^{\Delta \times \Delta}\) be a flat augmentation. In order for \(u\) to be an augmentation of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent, it suffices that \(X \circ L_i \xrightarrow{\ u * \mathrm{id}_{L_i}\ } C_S^\Delta\) (resp. \(X \circ c_i \xrightarrow{\ u * \mathrm{id}_{c_i}\ } C_S^\Delta\)) be so for every integer \(i\).
This follows from the explicit construction of \(\mathrm{R}_G^+\overline{u}_*\) (cf. (2.3.10)).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary (3.1.7)

Let \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\) be an augmentation; in order for \(u\) to be of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent, it is necessary and sufficient that \([[X\,|_{\mathrm{id}}\,X]] \longrightarrow C_S^{\Delta \times \Delta}\) be so.
3.2 Localization criteria

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (3.2.1)

Let \(Y \xrightarrow{\ v\ } C_S^\Delta\) be an augmentation of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent. In order for a flat augmentation \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\) to be of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent, it suffices that it become so after all the base changes \(Y_n \longrightarrow S\).

By means of the base changes \(Y_n \longrightarrow S\), we construct a double semi-simplicial object \(X \times_S Y\) augmented towards \(S\). By (3.1.4) and (3.1.5.1) the canonical morphism \(X \times_S Y \longrightarrow [[X\,|_{\mathrm{id}}\,X]]\) is an equivalence for \(G\)-1-cohomological descent: by virtue of (3.1.7), it suffices to show that the augmentation of \(X \times_S Y\) towards \(S\) is of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent. But this follows from the fact that the canonical morphism \(X \times_S Y \longrightarrow [[Y\,|_{\mathrm{id}}\,Y]]\) is an equivalence for \(G\)-1-cohomological descent: we again use (3.1.4), (3.1.5.1) and (3.1.7).

(3.2.2) Let \[ (3.2.2.1) \qquad \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ Y' \ar[r]^-{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & Y \ar[d]^{f} \\ X' \ar[r]_-{g} & X } \] be a commutative diagram in \(B\) and let \(F\) be an object of \(\underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}_S^{o}, \mathfrak{G}_S)\): there exists one and only one morphism \(\varphi(F) : g_*(f^*(F)) \longrightarrow f'^*(g'_*(F))\) such that the following diagram (in \(\underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}^{o}, \mathfrak{G})\)) commutes: \[ (3.2.2.2) \qquad \xymatrix@R=3em@C=1.6em{ f^*(F) \ar[rr] \ar[d] & & F \ar[d] \\ g_*(f^*(F)) \ar[dr] & & g'_*(F) \ar[dl] \\ & f'^*(g'_*(F)) & } \]

If we now suppose that all the arrows of (3.2.2.1) are flat, we define in the same way a morphism, called the base change morphism: \[ (3.2.2.3) \qquad \underline{g}_G : \mathrm{L}_G^+ g_* \circ \mathrm{R}_G^+ f^* \longrightarrow \mathrm{R}_G^+ f'^* \circ \mathrm{L}_G^+ g'_* \]

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.html:
Definition (3.2.2.4)

We say that the diagram (3.2.2.1) satisfies the base change theorem relative to \(G\) if \(f\), \(g\), \(f'\), \(g'\) are flat morphisms and if \(\underline{g}_G\) is an isomorphism.

(3.2.3) Let \(h : S \longrightarrow S'\) be a flat morphism in \(B\), and let \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\) and \(X' \xrightarrow{\ u'\ } C_{S'}^\Delta\) be two flat augmentations. Let \(f : X \longrightarrow X'\) be a functorial morphism such that the diagram (in \(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Delta^{o}, B)\)) \[ (3.2.3.1) \qquad \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X \ar[r]^-{f} \ar[d]_{u} & X' \ar[d]^{u'} \\ C_S^\Delta \ar[r]_-{h_c} & C_{S'}^\Delta } \] commutes. (\(h_c\) denotes the constant functorial morphism defined by \(h\)).

Let \(K'\) be a complex of \(\mathrm{D}^+(S')\): the morphism \[ \eta_G^f(K') : \mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}'_* \circ \mathrm{L}^+\overline{u}'^*(K') \longrightarrow \mathrm{R}^+(\overline{h_c \circ u})_* \circ \mathrm{L}^+(\overline{h_c \circ u})^*(K') \] induces, taking account of the identities: \[ \mathrm{R}^+(\overline{h_c \circ u})_* \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathrm{R}^+h_* \circ \mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}_* \quad \text{and} \quad \mathrm{L}^+(\overline{h_c \circ u})^* \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathrm{L}^+(\overline{u}^*) \circ \mathrm{L}^+h^* \] a morphism \(\mathrm{ch}_G^{f,h}(K')\), functorial in \(K'\), such that the following diagram commutes: \[ (3.2.3.2) \qquad \xymatrix@R=3.5em@C=1.2em{ \mathrm{L}_G^+h_* \circ \mathrm{R}_G^+\overline{u}'_* \circ \mathrm{L}_G^+\overline{u}'^*(K') \ar[rr]^-{\mathrm{ch}_G^{f,h}(K')} & & \mathrm{R}_G^+\overline{u}_* \circ \mathrm{L}_G^+\overline{u}^* \circ \mathrm{L}_G^+h_*(K') \\ & \mathrm{L}_G^+h_*(K') \ar[ul]^-{\mathrm{L}_G^+h_*(\alpha(K'))} \ar[ur]_-{\alpha(\mathrm{L}_G^+h_*(K'))} & } \]

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (3.2.3.3)

Suppose that, for every integer \(i\), the diagram \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X_i \ar[r]^-{f_i} \ar[d]_{u_i} & X'_i \ar[d]^{u'_i} \\ S \ar[r]_-{h} & S' } \] satisfies the base change theorem relative to \(G\). Then \(\mathrm{ch}_G^{f,h}\) is an isomorphism.

We may compute \(\mathrm{ch}_G^{f,h}(K')\) in the following way: we consider the augmentation \([X\,|_f\,X'] \xrightarrow{\ (h_c \circ u)_f\, u'\ } C_{S'}^\Delta\) (cf. (3.1.1.2)) and we choose a resolution \(J'\) of \(K^+(\overline{(h_c \circ u)fu'}^*)(K')\) such that, for every integer \(n\), \(J^n\) is totally acyclic object by object.

We obtain a quasi-isomorphism \[ \theta : K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(f^*))(r_o^*(J')) \longrightarrow r_1^*(J') \] and a morphism \[ t : K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(h_c^*)) \circ K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(u'_*))(r_o^*(J')) \longrightarrow K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(u_*))(r_1^*(J')) \] which admits the factorization: \[ K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(h_c^*)) \circ K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(u'_*))(r_o^*(J')) \xrightarrow{\ \varphi\ } K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(u_*)) \circ K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(f^*))(r_o^*(J')) \xrightarrow{\ K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(u_*))(\theta)\ } K^+(\underline{\Gamma}(u_*))(r_1^*(J')) \] and \(\mathrm{ch}_G^{f,h}(K')\) is obtained by taking the image of \(t\) under the functor \(\mathrm{R}^+\varepsilon_{Z'*}\).

Now, the preceding factorization shows that \(t\) is identified "object by object" with the base change morphisms relative to the diagrams: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X_i \ar[r]^-{f_i} \ar[d]_{u_i} & X'_i \ar[d]^{u'_i} \\ S \ar[r]_-{h} & S' } \] we deduce from this, by spectral sequences, that \(\mathrm{ch}_G^{f,h}(K')\) is an isomorphism, which completes the proof.
This leads us to a second localization criterion:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (3.2.4)

Let \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\) be an object of \(\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{plat}}(\Delta^{o}, B/S)\). In order for \(u\) to be an augmentation of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent, it suffices that it become so after "sufficiently many for \(G\)"(∗) flat base changes \(h : S' \longrightarrow S\) such that the cartesian diagrams \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X'_i \ar[r] \ar[d] & X_i \ar[d] \\ S' \ar[r]_-{h} & S } \] satisfy the base change theorem relative to \(G\).
Proposition (3.2.4) is evident from (3.2.3.3), taking account of the diagram (3.2.3.2).
3.3 Properties of morphisms of cohomological descent
In this section, we suppose that the set of flat morphisms in \(B\) is stable under base change.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (3.3.1)

\(i = 1, 2\).

  1. a)

    Every flat morphism which possesses a section is a morphism of universal \(G\)-2-cohomological descent.

  2. b)

    Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a flat morphism, \(g : S' \longrightarrow S\) a morphism of \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent, \(X' = X \times_S S'\), \(f' = f_{(S')} : X' \longrightarrow S'\). In order for \(f\) to be of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent, it is necessary and sufficient that \(f'\) be so.

  3. c)

    If the composite of two morphisms \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\), \(g : Y \longrightarrow Z\) is of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent, then \(g\) is of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent.

  4. d)

    The composite of two morphisms of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent is a morphism of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent.

  5. e)

    If \(f : X \longrightarrow X'\) and \(g : Y \longrightarrow Y'\) are two \(S\)-morphisms of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent, then \(f \times_S g\) is of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent.

  6. f)

    Let \((u_\alpha : X_\alpha \longrightarrow Y_\alpha)_{\alpha \in A}\) be a family of morphisms of \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent. Then \(\coprod u_\alpha : \coprod_{\alpha \in A} X_\alpha \longrightarrow \coprod_{\alpha \in A} Y_\alpha\) is a morphism of \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent.
Proof. As regards effective descent relative to \(G\) we refer to [4].

a) By means of a section \(s\) of \(f\) we compare the semi-simplicial objects augmented towards \(S\): \([X\,|_f\,S]\) and \([S\,|_{\mathrm{id}}\,S]\); thanks to (3.0.2.4) we obtain an equivalence for \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.
b) Follows from (3.2.1).
c) Follows from a) and b).

d) Let \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) and \(g : Y \longrightarrow S\) be two morphisms of universal \(G\)-1-cohomological descent. Set \(h = g \circ f\) and consider the fibre product: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ Y \ar[d]_{g} & R \ar[l]_-{h'} \ar[d]^{g'} \\ S & X \ar[l]^-{h} } \] \(g'\) possesses a section \(s : X \longrightarrow R\) such that \(h' \circ s = f\). By c), \(h'\) is of universal \(G\)-1-descent and the same holds for \(h\) by b).
e) Follows formally from b) and d).

f) Let \((Z_\lambda)_{\lambda \in \Lambda}\) be a family of objects of \(B\). It follows from the hypotheses (3.0.0) that we have a canonical equivalence \[ \underline{\mathrm{Mod}}\Big(\mathscr{E}_{\coprod_\lambda Z_\lambda}^{o}, \mathfrak{G}_{\coprod_\lambda Z_\lambda}\Big) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \prod_\lambda \underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}_{Z_\lambda}^{o}, \mathfrak{G}_{Z_\lambda}) \] inducing an equivalence \[ G_{\coprod_\lambda Z_\lambda} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \prod_\lambda G_{Z_\lambda} \] Moreover, if \((Q_\lambda)_\lambda \in \prod_\lambda \underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}_{Z_\lambda}^{o}, \mathfrak{G}_{Z_\lambda})\) is totally acyclic, then \(Q_\lambda\) is totally acyclic for every \(\lambda\).

Now let \((u_\lambda : X_\lambda \longrightarrow Y_\lambda)_{\lambda \in \Lambda}\) be a family of morphisms of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent: since the direct sums in \(B\) are disjoint and universal, we have for every \(n\) an identification \[ \Big[\coprod_\lambda X_\lambda \,\Big|_{\coprod_\lambda u_\lambda}\, \coprod_\lambda Y_\lambda\Big]_n \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \coprod_\lambda [X_\lambda \,|_{u_\lambda}\, Y_\lambda]_n \] which is functorial in \(n\). We then deduce from the preceding remarks and from the explicit computation of \(\mathrm{R}^+\overline{\theta}_*\) (cf. (2.3)) that \(\coprod_\lambda u_\lambda\) is a morphism of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent: the details are left to the reader. We also leave to the latter the task of verifying that \(\coprod_\lambda u_\lambda\) remains of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent after every base change if the same holds for \(u_\lambda\) for every \(\lambda\).

(3.3.2) If to each object \(X\) of \(B\) we associate the set of families of morphisms \((X_\alpha \longrightarrow X)_{\alpha \in A}\) such that \(\coprod_\alpha X_\alpha \longrightarrow X\) is a morphism of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent, we define, by virtue of (3.3.1), a pretopology on \(B\).

The topology generated by this pretopology is called the topology of \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent. It follows from \([(3.3.1)\text{-}c)]\) that the covering morphisms for this topology are exactly the morphisms of universal \(G\)-\(i\)-cohomological descent. Let us note finally that the topology of \(G\)-2-cohomological descent is coarser than the topology of \(G^{o}\)-descent [cf. [4] (6.23)].

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem (3.3.3)

Suppose that all the arrows of \(B\) are flat. Let \(S\) be an object of \(B\): every hypercovering of \(S\), for the topology of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent, all of whose objects are representable (cf. V appendix), defines an augmentation of universal \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.
The proof is carried out in two steps: let us specify that all the coskeletons will be computed in the category \(B/S\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (3.3.3.1)

Let \(X\) be an object of \(\mathrm{Hom}(\Delta^{o}, B/S)\); in order for \(X\) to be of 1-cohomological descent (resp. universal), it suffices that \(\mathrm{cosk}_n(X)\) be so for every \(n\) sufficiently large.

Indeed, let \(\alpha_n : X \longrightarrow \mathrm{cosk}_n(X)\) be the canonical morphism: one then verifies that if \(K'\) is a complex of \(\mathrm{D}_{G_S}^+(S)\) such that \(H^j(K') = 0\) for \(j < N\), then \(H^i(\eta_G^{\alpha_n})\) is an isomorphism for \(i < N+n\), whence the assertion.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (3.3.3.2)

Let \(n\) be an integer \(\geq 0\), and let \(X\) and \(X'\) be two simplicial objects of \(B/S\). Let \(f : X \longrightarrow X'\) be a morphism. We suppose that:

  1. (i)

    \(X \longrightarrow \mathrm{cosk}_{n+1}(X)\) is an isomorphism.

  2. (ii)

    \(X' \longrightarrow \mathrm{cosk}_{n+1}(X')\) is an isomorphism.

  3. (iii)

    \(f_i : X'_i \longrightarrow X_i\) is an isomorphism for \(i \leq n\).

  4. (iv)

    \(f_{n+1}\) is a morphism of universal \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.

Then if \(X\) is of universal \(G\)-1-cohomological descent, the same holds for \(X'\).
It is clear that (3.3.3.1) and (3.3.3.2) prove the theorem (3.3.3) by induction.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (3.3.3.3)

Under the hypotheses of (3.3.3.2), the morphisms \(f_p\) are all of universal \(G\)-1-cohomological descent

This is trivial for \(p \leq n+1\). For \(p > n+1\), \(X_p\) (resp. \(X'_p\)) can be written as \(\varprojlim_{\Delta^+_{n+1[p]}} X_q\) (resp. \(\varprojlim_{\Delta^+_{n+1[p]}} X'_q\)). Now for every arrow \(\iota : i \longrightarrow j\) of \(\Delta^+_{n+1[p]}\) we have a commutative diagram with exact rows: \[ \xymatrix@C=2.2em@R=2.8em{ K'_\iota \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\alpha'_\iota} & \displaystyle\prod_{r \in \mathrm{ob}(\Delta^+_{n+1[p]})} X'_2 \ar[r] & X'_j \ar[r] & X'_i \ar[d]^{f_i} \\ K_\iota \ar[r] & \displaystyle\prod_{\mathrm{ob}(\Delta^+_{n+1[p]})} X_2 \ar[r] & X_j \ar[r] & X_i } \] whose left square is cartesian (either \(i = n+1 = j\) and \(\iota = \mathrm{id}\), or \(i < n+1\) and \(f_i\) is an isomorphism). Then using (3.3.1) we see that \(\alpha_\iota\) is a morphism of universal \(G\)-1-cohomological descent. We complete the proof by remarking that \(f_p\) is identified with the canonical morphism \(\bigcap_\iota K'_\iota \xrightarrow{\ \times \alpha_\iota\ } \bigcap_\iota K_\iota\).

Let \([X'/X]^p\) be the \((p+1)\)-fold iterated fibre product of \(X'\) over \(X\). Thanks to (3.3.3.3), it suffices to verify (3.3.3.2) after a base change \([X'/X]^p \longrightarrow X\). After such a base change, the hypotheses of (3.3.3.2) are still satisfied, and moreover \(f_{n+1}\) admits a section. We may then apply (3.0.2.4) to complete the proof.
As regards effective descent, we have:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (3.3.4)

Let \(X : \Delta^{o} \longrightarrow B/S\) be a functor. Suppose that \(X_o \longrightarrow S\) is a morphism of universal \(G^{o}\)-2-descent, as are the morphisms \(X_{n+1} \longrightarrow (\mathrm{cosk}_n(X))_{n+1}\) for \(n = 0, 1\). Then the functor \(X\) is \(G^{o}\)-2-faithful and remains so after every base change (in other words \(X\) defines an augmentation of universal effective descent in the sense of (2.4.11)).
By [4] (7.12), it suffices to see that \(i_2^*(X)\) is \(G^{o}\)-2-faithful, and to do this we use the following lemmas:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (3.3.4.1)

Let \(X\) and \(X'\) be two functors \(\Delta_2^{o} \longrightarrow B/S\) and a commutative diagram: \[ \xymatrix@C=3em@R=2.8em{ X'_2 \ar@<0.8ex>[r] \ar[r] \ar@<-0.8ex>[r] \ar[d]_{k} & X'_1 \ar@<0.5ex>[r] \ar@<-0.5ex>[r] \ar@{=}[d] & X'_o \ar[r] \ar@{=}[d] & S \ar@{=}[d] \\ X_2 \ar@<0.8ex>[r] \ar[r] \ar@<-0.8ex>[r] & X_1 \ar@<0.5ex>[r] \ar@<-0.5ex>[r] & X_o \ar[r] & S } \] such that \(k\) is a morphism of \(G^{o}\)-0-descent. Then if \(X\) is \(G^{o}\)-2-faithful, the same holds for \(X'\).
Evident.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (3.3.4.2)

Let \(X\) and \(X'\) be two functors \(\Delta_2^{o} \longrightarrow B/S\) and a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix@C=3.2em@R=2.8em{ X'_2 \ar@<0.8ex>[r] \ar[r] \ar@<-0.8ex>[r] \ar[d]_{f_2} & X'_1 \ar@<0.5ex>[r]^{\partial^{o}} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_{\partial^1} \ar[d]^{f_1} & X'_o \ar[r] \ar@{=}[d] & S \ar@{=}[d] \\ X_2 \ar@<0.8ex>[r] \ar[r] \ar@<-0.8ex>[r] & X_1 \ar@<0.5ex>[r] \ar@<-0.5ex>[r] & X_o \ar[r] & S } \] such that \(f_1\) is of \(G^{o}\)-1-descent and \(f_2\) of \(G^{o}\)-0-descent. Suppose moreover that \(X'_2 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } (\mathrm{cosk})_1(X'))_2\). Then if \(X\) is \(G^{o}\)-2-faithful, the same holds for \(X'\).
Let \(X''_1 = X'_1 \times_{X_1} X'_1\), and let \(\partial_o : X''_1 \longrightarrow X'_1\) and \(\partial_1 : X''_1 \longrightarrow X'_1\) be the two projections.

Thanks to the definition of a coskeleton, we define an arrow \(\varphi : X''_1 \longrightarrow X'_2\) such that: \[ \begin{cases} \partial_o \circ \varphi = \underline{\partial}_o \\ \partial_1 \circ \varphi = \underline{\partial}_1 \\ \partial_2 \circ \varphi = \sigma_o \partial_1 \underline{\partial}_o = \sigma_o \partial_1 \underline{\partial}_1 \end{cases} \]

Now let a descent datum on \(X'\) be given; whence an object on \(X_o\), two objects on \(X_1\), an isomorphism between them on \(X'_1\). Thanks to \(\varphi\), we see that the two inverse images of these isomorphisms on \(X''_1\) are equal. Since \(f\) is of 1-descent, we obtain an isomorphism between the two objects on \(X_1\); this isomorphism is a descent datum (thanks to the fact that \(X'_2 \longrightarrow X_2\) is of 0-descent), and we are done.

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary (3.3.5)

Suppose that all the arrows of \(B\) are flat: every hypercovering of \(S\), for the topology of \(G\)-2-cohomological descent, whose objects are representable, defines an augmentation of universal \(G\)-2-cohomological descent.

footnotes.html: (∗) The expression "sufficiently many for \(G\)" means that there exists a family \((S_\alpha \xrightarrow{\ h_\alpha\ } S)_{\alpha \in A}\) of flat morphisms satisfying the preceding conditions and such that the family of functors \((h_{\alpha*} : G_S \to G_{S_\alpha})_{\alpha \in A}\) is conservative.

blocks.html: 4. Examples
4.1 Sheaves of abelian groups on topological spaces

(4.1.0) In this section \(\mathrm{Top}\) denotes the category of topological spaces [elements of the fixed universe \(\mathcal{U}\)]: we define a category \(\mathscr{E}\) bifibred in duals of topoi over \(\mathrm{Top}\) by taking as objects the pairs \((X, F)\), where \(X\) is a topological space and \(F\) a sheaf of sets on \(X\), and as morphisms the pairs \((f, \varphi) : (X, F) \longrightarrow (Y, H)\) where \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) is a continuous map and \(\varphi : H \longrightarrow f_*(F)\) a morphism of sheaves. For \(\mathfrak{G}\) we take the section of \(\mathscr{E}^{o}\) over \(\mathrm{Top}^{o}\) which associates to each topological space the constant sheaf \(\mathbf{Z}_X\): we shall set \(G = \underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}^{o}, \mathfrak{G})\) so that, for every topological space \(X\), \(G_X\) is identified with the category of sheaves of abelian groups on \(X\).

Let us recall that a morphism \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) is separated if the diagonal of \(X \times_Y X\) is closed. A proper morphism is a separated and universally closed morphism (be careful that this definition is more restrictive than that of Bourbaki).
The proof of the "base change theorem" below is inspired by \(([5] II (4.11.1))\).

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem (4.1.1)

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a proper morphism, \(F\) an abelian sheaf on \(X\) and a cartesian diagram \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X' \ar[r]^-{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^{f} \\ Y' \ar[r]_-{g} & Y } \] Then the canonical map (XII 4.2) or (3.2.2.3) \[ g^* \mathrm{R}^i f_* F \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathrm{R}^i f'_* g'^* F \] is an isomorphism.
This theorem is equivalent to the following corollary (the corollary is obtained by setting \(Y' = (\text{Point})\); the theorem is obtained by applying the corollary to \(f\) and \(f'\)).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary (4.1.2)

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a proper morphism, \(F\) an abelian sheaf on \(X\) and \(y \in Y\). The canonical map \[ (\mathrm{R}^i f_* F)_y \longrightarrow H^i(f^{-1}(y), F) \] is bijective.

By definition, for \(U\) ranging over the neighbourhoods of \(Y\), we have \[ (\mathrm{R}^i f_* F)_y = \varinjlim_U H^i(f^{-1}(U), F) . \] Since \(f\) is closed, the \(f^{-1}(U)\) form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of \(f^{-1}(y)\) and (4.1.3) follows from the following lemma.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (4.1.3)

Let \(X\) be a topological space, \(K \subset X\) and \(F\) an abelian sheaf on \(X\). Suppose that \(K\) is compact and that any two distinct points of \(K\) have, in \(X\), disjoint neighbourhoods. Then, for \(U\) ranging over the neighbourhoods of \(K\), we have \[ (4.1.3.1) \qquad \varinjlim_U H^i(U, F) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^i(K, F) \]
We shall first treat the case \(i = 0\). In this case, it is clear that (4.1.3.1) is injective. For the surjectivity, we shall use:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (4.1.4)

Under the hypotheses of (4.1.3), if \(A\) and \(B\) are two closed subsets of \(K\) and \(W\) a neighbourhood of \(A \cap B\) in \(X\), there exist neighbourhoods \(U\) and \(V\) of \(A\) and \(B\) in \(X\) such that \(U \cap V \subset W\).

We shall first treat the case where \(A\) is reduced to a single point \(a\). The assertion is trivial if \(a \in B\) (take \(U = W\)). If \(a \notin B\) then for each \(b \in B\) there exist disjoint open neighbourhoods \(U_b\) and \(V_b\) of \(a\) and \(b\) in \(X\). We take for \(V\) a finite union of the \(V_b\) covering \(B\), and for \(U\) the intersection of the corresponding \(U_b\).

In the general case, for each \(a \in A\), there exist open neighbourhoods \(U_a\) and \(V_a\) of \(a\) and \(B\) in \(X\) with \(U_a \cap V_a \subset W\). We take for \(U\) a finite union of the \(U_a\), which covers \(A\), and for \(V\) the corresponding intersection of the \(V_a\).

Let us return to (4.1.3). If \(s \in H^0(K, F)\), there exist an open covering \(U_i\) of \(K\) in \(X\) and \(s_i \in H^0(U_i, F)\) such that \(s_i = s\) on \(U_i \cap K\). We may assume the \(U_i\) to be finite in number. Let \((K_i)\) be a closed covering of \(K\), with \(K_i \subset K \cap U_i\). Let \(W_y\) be the open set of \(U_i \cap U_j\) where \(s_i = s_j\); we have \(K_i \cap K_j \subset W_{ij}\). Let us apply (4.1.4) to all the pairs \((K_i, K_j)\) and to the \(W_{ij}\): we find open sets \(V_{ij}\) with \(K_i \subset V_{ij} \subset U_i\) and \(V_{ij} \cap V_{ji} \subset W_{ij}\). Let \(U'_i = \bigcap_j V_{ij}\): we have \(K_i \subset U'_i \subset U_i\), and \(s_i = s_j\) on \(U'_i \cap U'_j\). The \(s_i\) thus glue together on the neighbourhood of \(K\) which is the union of the \(U'_i\), and (4.1.3.1) is surjective (hence bijective) for \(i = 0\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (4.1.5)

If \(F\) is flasque, then the sheaf \(F|_K\) on \(K\) is soft.
Let \(A \subset K\) be a closed subset in \(K\). Every section of \(F\) on \(A\) extends to a neighbourhood, by what precedes. Since \(F\) is flasque, it extends to \(X\), and a fortiori to \(K\).

Let us prove (4.1.3). Let \(F^*\) be a flasque resolution of \(F\). We have \[ \varinjlim_U H^i(U, F) = \varinjlim_U H^i(\Gamma(U, F^*)) = H^i \varinjlim_U \Gamma(U, F^*) = H^i \Gamma(K, F^*) = H^i(K, F) . \] (the equality \(H^i \varinjlim_U \Gamma(U, F^*) = H^i \Gamma(K, F^*)\) follows from (4.1.3) for \(i = 0\), cf. (4.1.5)).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary (4.1.6)

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a proper and surjective morphism of topological spaces. Then \(f\) is of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.
Follows from (4.1.2) and (3.2.4).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary (4.1.7)

Let \(\mathfrak{u} = (U_i)_{i \in I}\) be a locally finite closed covering of a topological space \(X\). Then the canonical morphism \(f : \coprod_{i \in I} U_i \longrightarrow X\) is a morphism of \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.
Indeed \(f\) is proper and surjective. Applying (2.5.6), we recover the spectral sequence of \([[5] II (5.2.4)]\) (cf. the introduction).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (4.1.8)

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a surjective local homeomorphism of topological spaces. Then \(f\) is a morphism of universal \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.
By localization on \(Y\) (cf. (3.2.4)), we are reduced to the case where \(f\) possesses a section.

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary (4.1.9)

Let \(\mathfrak{u} = (U_i)_{i \in I}\) be an open covering of a topological space \(X\). Then the canonical morphism \(f : \coprod_{i \in I} U_i \longrightarrow X\) is a morphism of universal \(G\)-1-cohomological descent.
The descent spectral sequence then gives \([[5] II (5.4.1)]\) (cf. the Introduction).
The proofs of (VIII. 9) show that one can replace "1-cohomological descent" by "2-cohomological descent" in all the statements that precede.
4.2 Quasi-coherent modules on schemes

(4.2.0) Let \((\mathrm{Sch})_S\) be the category whose objects are the schemes that are elements of \(\mathcal{U}\) and whose arrows are the quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms: we define a category \(\mathscr{E}\) bifibred in duals of topoi over \((\mathrm{Sch})_S\) by taking as objects the pairs \((X, F)\) where \(X\) is a scheme and \(F\) a sheaf on \(X\) (for the Zariski topology), and as morphisms the pairs \((f, \varphi) : (X, F) \longrightarrow (Y, G)\), where \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) is a continuous map and \(\varphi : G \longrightarrow f_*(F)\) a morphism of sheaves. For \(\mathfrak{G}\) we take the section of \(\mathscr{E}^{o}\) over \((\mathrm{Sch})^{o}\) which associates to each scheme its structure sheaf; for \(G\) we take the subcategory of \(\underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}^{o}, \mathfrak{G})\) such that for every scheme \(X\), \(G_X\) is the category of quasi-coherent modules on \(X\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (4.2.1)

Every faithfully flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) is a morphism of universal \(G\)-2-cohomological descent.

By \([\mathrm{S.G.A\ I\ (VIII\ 5.2)}]\), \(f\) is a morphism of effective \(G^{o}\)-descent. By virtue of \([\mathrm{E.G.A\ IV\ (1.7.21)}]\), we may apply (3.2.4) to the cartesian square: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X \times_Y X \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d]^{f} \\ X \ar[r]_-{f} & Y } \]
4.3 Étale sheaves on schemes

(4.3.0) Let \((\mathrm{Sch})\) be the category of all schemes belonging to \(\mathcal{U}\): we thus define a category \(\mathscr{E}\) bifibred in duals of topoi over \((\mathrm{Sch})\) by taking as objects the pairs \((X, F)\), where \(X\) is a scheme and \(F\) an étale sheaf on \(X\), and as morphisms the pairs \((f, \varphi) : (X, F) \longrightarrow (Y, G)\), where \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) is a morphism of schemes and \(\varphi : G \longrightarrow f_*(F)\) is a morphism of sheaves.

Let \(n\) be an integer \(\geq 0\): we denote by \(\mathfrak{G}_n\) the section of \(\mathscr{E}^{o}\) over \((\mathrm{Sch})^{o}\) which associates to each scheme \(X\) the constant sheaf \((\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z})_X\). We shall set \(F_n = \underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}^{o}, \mathfrak{G}_n)\) so that, for every scheme \(X\), \(F_{n_X}\) is identified with the category of sheaves of \(\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z}\)-modules on \(X\).

(4.3.1) Now let \((\mathrm{Sch})_S\) be the subcategory of \((\mathrm{Sch})\) whose objects are the schemes that are elements of \(\mathcal{U}\) and whose arrows are the quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms. We denote by \(\mathscr{E}_S\) the category bifibred in duals of topoi over \((\mathrm{Sch})_S\) deduced from \(\mathscr{E}\) by the base change \((\mathrm{Sch})_S \longrightarrow (\mathrm{Sch})\); we again denote by \(\mathfrak{G}_o\) the restriction of \(\mathfrak{G}_o\) to \((\mathrm{Sch})_S\). Let \(G \subset \underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}_S^{o}, \mathfrak{G}_o)\) be the fibred and cofibred subcategory of \(\underline{\mathrm{Mod}}(\mathscr{E}_S^{o}, \mathfrak{G}_o)\) such that for every scheme \(X\), \(G_X\) is the category of abelian torsion sheaves on \(X\): the reader will note that the condition (2.4.1.1) is satisfied.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (4.3.2)

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a proper surjective morphism. Then \(f\) is a morphism of universal cohomological \(F_n\)-2-descent for \(n \geq 1\). Considered as a morphism of \((\mathrm{Sch})_S\), \(f\) is a morphism of universal cohomological \(G\)-2-descent.

By (VIII. (9.4)) \(f\) is a morphism of effective \(F^{o}\)-descent, and by (XII. (5.1)), we may apply (3.2.4) to the cartesian diagram: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X \times_Y X \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d]^{f} \\ X \ar[r]_-{f} & Y } \]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (4.3.3)

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a surjective morphism of schemes. Suppose that one of the following hypotheses is satisfied:

  1. a)

    \(f\) is integral.

  2. b)

    \(Y\) is locally noetherian, \(f\) is universally open and locally of finite presentation.

  3. c)

    \(f\) is flat and locally of finite presentation.

Then \(f\) is a morphism of cohomological \(F_n\)-2-descent, for all \(n \geq 0\).
a) We copy the proof of (4.3.2), replacing (XII. (5.1)) by (VIII. (5.6)).

b) Since the question is local on \(Y\), we may assume that \(Y\) is noetherian. We apply (E.G.A. IV. (14.5.10)). By (3.3.1) and a), we reduce to the case where every point \(y\) of \(Y\) has a neighbourhood \(U\) such that \(f^{-1}(U) \longrightarrow U\) has a section, and we conclude by (3.2.4).
c) We must show that \(f\) is a morphism of cohomological \(F\)-1-descent (we know by (VIII. (9.4)) that \(f\) is a morphism of effective \(F^{o}\)-descent).

By localization on \(Y\) (cf. (3.2.4)), we may assume that \(Y\) is affine with ring \(A\). We may then write \(\operatorname{Spec} A = \varprojlim_{i \in I} \operatorname{Spec} A_i\), where \(I\) is a filtered ordered set and \(A_i\) a noetherian ring for every \(i\), with \(X = \varprojlim X_i\), where, for every \(i\), \(X_i\) is a scheme flat and locally of finite presentation over \(\operatorname{Spec} A_i\) such that \(f_i : X_i \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec} A_i\) is surjective; moreover, the diagrams: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X \ar[r] \ar[d]_{f} & X_i \ar[d]^{f_i} \\ Y \ar[r]_-{u_i} & \operatorname{Spec} A_i } \] are cartesian.

Let \(\mathfrak{F}\) be an abelian sheaf on \(Y\): we have \(\mathfrak{F} = \varinjlim_i u_i^* u_{i*}(\mathfrak{F})\), so that, by a standard passage to the limit, we are reduced to the case where \(\mathfrak{F}\) comes from a sheaf on \(\operatorname{Spec} A_i\) for some \(i\), and b) allows us to conclude.

If \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) is integral, we have \(\mathrm{R}^q f_* = 0\) for \(q > 0\). We easily conclude that it is not necessary to restrict to bounded-below complexes in order to perform descent by means of \(f\).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary (4.3.5)

Let \((X_\alpha \xrightarrow{\ u_\alpha\ } X)_{\alpha \in A}\) be a covering family for the étale topology. Then \(\coprod_{\alpha \in A} X_\alpha \longrightarrow X\) is a morphism of universal cohomological \(F_n\)-2-descent for all \(n \geq 0\).
Indeed, there exists a factorization \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=1em{ & \coprod_{\alpha \in A} X_\alpha \ar[dr] & \\ X \ar[rr]_-{h} \ar[ur] & & X } \] where \(h\) is a surjective étale morphism.
5. Applications
5.1 Construction of simplicial objects

(5.1.0) Up to and including number (5.1.3), \(H\) is a category in which finite non-empty projective limits exist and in which finite sums exist, are disjoint and universal. If \(X : \Delta^{o} \longrightarrow H\) is a simplicial object of \(H\), we shall denote by \(d_i^k : X_k \longrightarrow X_{k-1}\) (resp. \(s_i^k : X_k \longrightarrow X_{k+1}\)) for \(i \in [k]\) and \(0 \leq k\) the arrows corresponding to the "face" operators \(\partial_k^i : [k-1] \longrightarrow [k]\) (resp. to the degeneracy operators \(\sigma_k^i : [k] \longrightarrow [k+1]\)) (cf. [3] II 2).

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.html:
Definition (5.1.1)

A simplicial object \(X : \Delta^{o} \longrightarrow H\) of \(H\) is \(\sigma\)-split if there exists a family of subobjects \(NX_j\) of the \(X_j\) (\(j \geq 0\)) such that the morphisms \[ h_i : \coprod_{\substack{\mathrm{Hom}_{\Delta^-}([i], [j]) \\ j \leq i}} NX_j \longrightarrow X_i \] are isomorphisms.

Likewise, a \(k\)-truncated simplicial object \(X : \Delta_k^{o} \longrightarrow H\) is \(\sigma\)-split if there exist \(NX_j\) (\(0 \leq j \leq k\)) satisfying the preceding condition for \(i \leq k\).

The \(NX_j\) are uniquely determined by \(X\). Indeed, if \(X\) is \(\sigma\)-split, the degeneracy operators \(s_\iota^{k-1} : X_{k-1} \longrightarrow X_k\) are isomorphisms of \(X_{k-1}\) onto direct factors of \(X_k\), and \[ NX_k = \bigcap_\iota (\text{complement of } s_\iota^k(X_{k-1})) . \] For \(k = 0\), \(NX_o = X_o\).
(5.1.2) For \(X\) an \((n+1)\)-truncated \(\sigma\)-split simplicial object of \(H\), we shall denote by \(\alpha_n(X)\) the triple consisting of

1. a)

    the restriction \(i_n^*(X)\) of \(X\) to \(\Delta_n^{o}\).

  2. b)

    \(NX_{n+1}\),

  3. c)

    the obvious map from \(NX_{n+1}\) into \((\mathrm{cosq}_n(X))_{n+1}\)
This triple \((Y, N, \beta)\) satisfies the following condition:
(*) \(Y\) is an \(n\)-truncated \(\sigma\)-split simplicial object of \(H\), and \(\beta\) is a map from \(N\) into \((\mathrm{cosq}\, Y)_{n+1}\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (5.1.3)

Let \((Y, N, \beta)\) be a triple satisfying (*) above.

  1. (i)

    Up to unique isomorphism, there exists one and only one \(\sigma\)-split \(X : \Delta_{n+1}^{o} \longrightarrow H\), with \(\alpha_n(X) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } (Y, N, \beta)\),

  2. (ii)

    Giving a morphism \(f\) from \(X\) into a truncated simplicial object \(Z : \Delta_{n+1}^{o} \longrightarrow H\) amounts to the same thing as giving

    1. a)

      a morphism \(f' : Y \longrightarrow i_n^*(Z)\);

    2. b)

      a morphism \(f'' : N \longrightarrow Z_{n+1}\) such that the diagram \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ N \ar[r] \ar[d]_{f''} & (\mathrm{cosq}_n Y)_{n+1} \ar[d]^{f'} \\ Z_{n+1} \ar[r] & (\mathrm{cosq}_n Z)_{n+1} } \] is commutative.
Let us construct \(X\).

We set \(Y'_n = (\mathrm{cosk}_n Y)_{n+1}\) and denote by \(d'^{n+1}_i : Y'_{n+1} \longrightarrow Y_n\) (resp. \(s'^n_i : Y_n \longrightarrow Y'_{n+1}\)) the face (resp. degeneracy) operators obtained by functoriality.

+ We set \(Y_{n+1} = N \amalg \Big(\coprod_{\substack{\mathrm{Hom}_{\Delta^-}([n+1], [\iota]) \\ \iota \leq n}} NY_\iota\Big)\) and let \(\alpha : Y_{n+1} \longrightarrow Y'_{n+1}\) be the arrow whose components are \(\beta\) and the arrows \(NY_\iota \longrightarrow Y'_{n+1}\) for every epimorphism \([n+1] \longrightarrow [\iota]\) with \(\iota \leq n\).

+ Let \(s_i^n : Y_n \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \coprod_{\substack{\mathrm{Hom}_{\Delta^-}([n], [\iota']) \\ \iota' \leq n}} NY_{\iota'} \longrightarrow X_{n+1}\) be the arrow induced by \(\sigma_n^i\), so that \[ \text{(I)} \qquad \alpha \circ s_i^n = s'^n_i . \] We set \[ \text{(II)} \qquad d_i^{n+1} = d'^{n+1}_i \circ \alpha . \]

+ To show that we thereby define an object of \(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Delta_{n+1}^{o}, H)\), it suffices, by \([[3]. II(2.4)]\), to verify the formulas \[ \text{a)} \qquad d_i^n \cdot d_j^{n+1} = d_{j-1}^n \cdot d_i^{n+1} \qquad i < j \] \[ \text{b)} \qquad s_i^n \cdot s_j^{n-1} = s_{j+1}^n \cdot s_i^{n-1} \qquad i \leq j \] \[ \text{c)} \qquad d_i^{n+1} \cdot s_j^n = \begin{cases} s_{j-1}^{n-1} \cdot d_i^n & i < j \\ \mathrm{id} & i = j \text{ or } i = j+1 \\ s_j^{n-1} \cdot d_{i-1}^n & i > j+1 \end{cases} \]
Formulas a) and c) are obvious by virtue of (I) and (II), since we know that a) and c) are satisfied if we replace \(d_i^{n+1}\) by \(d'^{n+1}_i\) and \(s_i^n\) by \(s'^n_i\).
Formula b) is satisfied by construction.
We leave to the reader the task of verifying that the object \(X\) obtained satisfies 5.1.3.

+ One should note that the functor constructed in the proof of 5.1.3, from the category of triples satisfying (5.1.2) (*) into the \(n{+}1\)-truncated simplicial objects, is faithful but not fully faithful.

Proposition 5.1.3 provides a very convenient procedure for constructing simplicial objects of \(H\) by induction. In the remainder of this number, we formalize this remark in the form that will be used in 5.2 and 5.3.
(5.1.4) Let \(E \xrightarrow{\ \pi\ } B\) be a functor such that for every object \(b\) of \(B\), the fibre category \(E_b\) is non-empty and satisfies the conditions of (5.1.0).
Let \(Q\) be a property of an object of \(E\), stable under isomorphism: we suppose that the following conditions are fulfilled:

1. a)

    For every object \(b\) of \(B\), there exists an object \(x\) of \(E_b\) satisfying \(Q\).

  2. b)

    For every object \(b\) of \(B\) and every pair \((x, y)\) of objects of \(E_b\) satisfying \(Q\), there exists an object \(z\) of \(E_b\) satisfying \(Q\) and morphisms \(z \longrightarrow x\), \(z \longrightarrow y\) in \(E_b\).

  3. c)

    For every morphism \(b' \xrightarrow{\ t\ } b\) of \(B\) and every object \(x\) of \(E_b\) satisfying \(Q\), there exists an object \(x'\) of \(E_{b'}\), satisfying \(Q\), and a morphism \(x' \longrightarrow x\) over \(t\).
Let \(P\), on the other hand, be a property of an arrow of \(E\) over an identity, stable under isomorphism: we suppose that the following conditions are fulfilled:

1. d)

    For every object \(b\) of \(B\) and every object \(x\) of \(E_b\), there exists an arrow \(y \longrightarrow x\) in \(E_b\) satisfying \(P\).

  2. e)

    For every object \(G\) of \(B\), every diagram in \(E_b\) of the form \[ \xymatrix@R=1.6em@C=2.5em{ u \ar[rr]^-{f} & & x \\ & z \ar[ur] \ar[dr] & \\ v \ar[rr]_-{g} & & y } \] where \(f\) and \(g\) satisfy \(P\), can be completed to a commutative diagram in \(E_b\) \[ \xymatrix@R=1.6em@C=2.5em{ u \ar[rr]^-{f} & & x \\ w \ar[r]^-{h} \ar[u] \ar[d] & z \ar[ur] \ar[dr] & \\ v \ar[rr]_-{g} & & y } \] where \(h\) satisfies \(P\).

  3. f)

    For every morphism \(b' \xrightarrow{\ t\ } b\) of \(B\) and every morphism \(x \xrightarrow{\ f\ } y\) of \(E_b\) satisfying \(P\), there exists a morphism \(x' \xrightarrow{\ f'\ } y'\) of \(E_{b'}\), satisfying \(P\), and a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ x' \ar[r]^-{\alpha} \ar[d]_{f'} & x \ar[d]^{f} \\ y' \ar[r]_-{\beta} & y } \] where \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are morphisms over \(t\).

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.html:
Definition (5.1.5)

With the notations of (5.1.4), we shall say that an object \(X\) of \(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Delta^{o}, E)\) satisfies condition (APQ) if the following conditions are fulfilled:

  1. (i)

    The image of \(\pi \circ X\) is the constant simplicial object defined by an object \(G\) of \(B\).

  2. (ii)

    As an object of \(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Delta^{o}, E_b)\), \(X\) is \(\sigma\)-split.

  3. (iii)

    \(X_o\) satisfies condition \(Q\).

  4. (iv)

    For every integer \(n\), the arrow \(NX_{n+1} \longrightarrow (\mathrm{cosq}_n X)_{n+1}\) satisfies condition \(P\).

(5.1.6) We denote by \(E_{(APQ)}\) the subcategory of \(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Delta^{o}, E)\) whose objects are the simplicial objects satisfying (APQ) and whose morphisms are the morphisms \(X \xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ } Y\) of \(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Delta^{o}, E)\) such that \(\pi(\alpha_n) : \pi(X_n) \longrightarrow \pi(Y_n)\) is the same morphism of \(B\) for every \(n\). There then exists a canonical functor \[ \overline{\pi} : E_{(APQ)} \longrightarrow B . \]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (5.1.7)

The functor \(\overline{\pi}\) is surjective. Moreover, for every object \(b\) of \(B\) and every pair \((X, Y)\) of objects of \(E_{(APQ),b}\), there exists a diagram \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=1.5em{ & Z \ar[dl] \ar[dr] & \\ X & & Y } \] in \(E_{(APQ),b}\).
The proof is trivial from (5.1.3), by virtue of the hypotheses made in (5.1.4).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (5.1.8)

Let \(C\) be a category and \(F\) a functor \(E_{(APQ)} \longrightarrow C\); we introduce the following conditions for \(F\):

  1. (i)

    For every object \(b\) of \(B\), the restriction of \(F\) to \(E_{(APQ),b}\) factors through the coarse category(∗) defined by the objects of \(E_{(APQ),b}\).

  2. (ii)

    For every morphism \(t : b' \longrightarrow b\) of \(B\) and every pair \((X' \longrightarrow X, Y' \longrightarrow Y)\) of morphisms over \(t\), the following diagram is commutative: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ F(X') \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\alpha'} & F(X) \ar[d]^{\alpha} \\ F(Y') \ar[r] & F(Y) } \] where \(\alpha\) and \(\alpha'\) are the arrows determined by condition (i).

Then, the functor \(G \longmapsto G \circ \overline{\pi}\) induces an equivalence between the category \(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(B, C)\) and the full subcategory of \(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(E_{(APQ)}, C)\) defined by the functors satisfying conditions (i) and (ii).
The details of the proof are left to the reader. Let us simply indicate the manner in which one proceeds to show that the preceding functor is essentially surjective.

Let \(F : E_{(APQ)} \longrightarrow C\) be a functor satisfying conditions (i) and (ii); for every object \(b\) of \(B\), we choose an object \(X\) of \(E_{(APQ),b}\) and set \(\overline{F}(b) = F(X)\); we then verify that \(\overline{F}(b)\) varies functorially with \(b\).
5.2 Singular cohomology of a scheme of finite type over a field of characteristic zero
In this number, \(k\) will denote a field of characteristic zero.

(5.2.0) We shall denote by \(\mathrm{Sch}_f/k\) (resp. \(\mathrm{Ann}\)) the category of schemes locally of finite type over \(k\) (resp. of complex analytic spaces). All the simplicial objects of \(\mathrm{Sch}_f/k\) (resp. \(\mathrm{Ann}\)) will be considered as simplicial objects of \(\mathrm{Top}\) by means of the canonical functor \(\mathrm{Sch}_f/k \to \mathrm{Top}\) (resp. \(\mathrm{Ann} \to \mathrm{Top}\)). We retain the data of (4.1.0) relating to cohomological descent.
Following the usual notations, we shall denote by \(S \longrightarrow S^{\mathrm{an}}\) the canonical functor \(\mathrm{Sch}_f/\mathbf{C} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ann}\) defined in G.A.G.A.

(5.2.1) Let \(X\) be a simplicial object of \(\mathrm{Sch}/k\) (resp. \(\mathrm{Ann}\)): the usual compatibilities for the construction of the De Rham complex of a morphism of schemes (resp. of analytic spaces) allow one to construct a complex \(\Omega^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{X/k}\) (resp. \(\Omega_{X/\mathbf{C}}\)) of \(\mathrm{D}^+(\underline{\Gamma}(\overline{X}), \mathbf{Z})\) such that for every integer \(i\), \(\mathrm{R}^+e_i^*(\Omega^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{X/k})\) (resp. \(\mathrm{R}^+e_i^*(\Omega_{X_i/\mathbf{C}})\)) is the De Rham complex \(\Omega^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{X_i/k}\) (resp. \(\Omega_{X_i/\mathbf{C}}\)).

Let \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\) be a simplicial object of \(\mathrm{Sch}_f/k\) (resp. \(\mathrm{Ann}\)) equipped with an augmentation. We define \(H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}(u)\) (resp. \(H_{\mathrm{DR}}(u)\) and \(H(u, \mathbf{C})\)) as the hypercohomology groups of the complex \(\mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}_*(\Omega^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{X/k})\) (resp. \(\mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}_*(\Omega_{X/\mathbf{C}})\) and \(\mathrm{R}^+\overline{u}_*(\mathbf{C})\)).

(5.2.2) If \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\) is a semi-simplicial object of \(\mathrm{Sch}_f/\mathbf{C}\), one has three canonical morphisms: \[ H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}(u) \xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ } H_{\mathrm{DR}}(u^{\mathrm{an}}) \] \[ H(u^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbf{C}) \xrightarrow{\ \beta\ } H_{\mathrm{DR}}(u^{\mathrm{an}}) \] \[ H(S^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbf{C}) \xrightarrow{\ \gamma\ } H(u^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbf{C}) \]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (5.2.3)

Suppose, with the notations of (5.2.2), that \(X_n\) is smooth for every \(n\): then \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are isomorphisms. If moreover \(X^{\mathrm{an}} \xrightarrow{\ u^{\mathrm{an}}\ } C_{S^{\mathrm{an}}}^\Delta\) is a hypercovering of \(S^{\mathrm{an}}\) for the topology of universal cohomological 1-descent, then \(\gamma\) is an isomorphism.

The fact that \(\alpha\) is an isomorphism follows from \([[6]. \text{Th. } 1']\). It follows from the Poincaré lemma that \(\beta\) is an isomorphism. The last part of the proposition follows from (3.3.3).

(5.2.4) We shall now apply (5.1.4) to the case where \(B = \mathrm{Sch}_f/k\) and where \(E\) is the category over \(B\) such that for every scheme \(S\), the fibre category \(E_S\) is the category of schemes of \(\mathrm{Sch}_f/k\) over \(S\), the arrows over an arrow of \(B\) being the obvious ones. We shall say that a morphism \(h : X \longrightarrow Y\) over \(S\) satisfies property \(P\) if \(X\) is smooth over \(k\) and if \(h\) is composed of a finite number of morphisms satisfying one of the following conditions:

1. (i)

    being the sum of a family of étale and surjective morphisms

  2. (ii)

    being the sum of a family of proper and surjective morphisms.
We shall say that a scheme \(X\) of \(E_S\) satisfies property \(Q\) if the structural morphism \(X \longrightarrow S\) satisfies property \(P\).
We leave to the reader the task of verifying, via resolution of singularities, that all the conditions of (5.1.4) are satisfied.

The datum of the groups \(H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}(u)\) defines a contravariant functor from the category \(E_{(APQ)}\) into the category of graded abelian groups, denoted \(H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (5.2.5)

The functor \(H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}\) satisfies the conditions of (5.1.8).

By the Lefschetz principle, we are reduced to the case where \(k = \mathbf{C}\). In this case, for every morphism \(S' \xrightarrow{\ t\ } S\) and every pair \((u' \longrightarrow u, v' \longrightarrow v)\) of morphisms over \(t\), one has a commutative diagram: \[ \xymatrix@R=3em@C=3.5em{ H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}(u') \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\gamma^{-1}\cdot\beta^{-1}\cdot\alpha} & H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}(u) \ar[d]^{\gamma^{-1}\cdot\beta^{-1}\cdot\alpha} \\ H(S'^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbf{C}) \ar[r]^-{H(t^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbf{C})} & H(S^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbf{C}) \\ H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}(v') \ar[r] \ar[u]^{\gamma^{-1}\cdot\beta^{-1}\cdot\alpha} & H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}(v) \ar[u]_{\gamma^{-1}\cdot\beta^{-1}\cdot\alpha} } \] which completes the proof.

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.html:
Definition (5.2.6)

The contravariant functor defined by (5.1.8) from \(H^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{\mathrm{DR}}\) will be denoted \(H(*, k)\). For every scheme \(S\) locally of finite type over \(k\), the graded abelian group \(H(S, k)\) will be called the singular cohomology of \(S\).

(5.2.7) We shall conclude this number with an illustration of the general principles that have been introduced in it. Let us first recall that if \(S\) is a complex analytic space, the De Rham cohomology of \(S\), denoted \(H^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{DR}}(S)\), is by definition the hypercohomology of the De Rham complex \(\Omega^{\bullet}_{S/\mathbf{C}}\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (5.2.8) (Blum-Herrera)

Let \(S\) be a scheme locally of finite type over \(\mathbf{C}\); the canonical arrow \[ H(S^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbf{C}) \longrightarrow H^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{DR}}(S^{\mathrm{an}}) \] has a retraction (in the category of graded abelian groups) functorial in \(S\).

By virtue of (5.1.8), it suffices to consider the morphism \(H(*, \mathbf{C}) \circ \overline{\pi} \longrightarrow H^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{DR}} \circ \overline{\pi}\) obtained from the preceding one by composition with \(\overline{\pi}\).

Using, for every augmentation \(X \xrightarrow{\ u\ } C_S^\Delta\), the canonical morphism \(\mathrm{L}^+\overline{u}^*(\Omega^{\bullet}_{S/\mathbf{C}}) \longrightarrow \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/\mathbf{C}}\), we define a functorial morphism \(H^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{DR}} \circ \overline{\pi} \longrightarrow H^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{DR}}\), so that the following diagram is commutative: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=2.5em{ H^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{DR}} & & H^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{DR}} \circ \overline{\pi} \ar[ll] \\ & H(*, \mathbf{C}) \circ \overline{\pi} \ar[ul]^{\beta \circ \gamma} \ar[ur] & } \] which provides the sought retraction.
The statement (5.2.8) remains valid for every analytic space, as soon as one has resolution of singularities in the analytic setting.
5.3 Mixed Hodge theories
We give here a result of a technical nature that plays a key role in [2].
\(k\) is a field of characteristic zero.

(5.3.1) Let \(\mathrm{Sch}_{fs}/k\) be the category of schemes separated and of finite type over \(k\); we denote by \(E \xrightarrow{\ \pi\ } \mathrm{Sch}_{fs}/k\) the category over \(\mathrm{Sch}_{fs}/k\) defined in the following manner:

+ If \(S\) is an object of \(\mathrm{Sch}_{fs}/k\), an object of \(E_S\) is a triple \((\overline{X}, X, i)\) where \(\overline{X}\) is a reduced projective scheme over \(k\), \(X\) a proper scheme over \(S\), and \(i : X \longrightarrow \overline{X}\) an open immersion over \(k\) such that \(i(X)\) is dense in \(\overline{X}\).

+ If \(t : S' \longrightarrow S\) is a morphism of schemes, \((\overline{X}, X, i)\) an object over \(S\), and \((\overline{X}', X', i')\) an object over \(S'\), a morphism from \((\overline{X}, X, i)\) into \((\overline{X}', X', i')\) over \(t\) is a pair \((\overline{h}, h)\) where \(\overline{h} : \overline{X}' \longrightarrow \overline{X}\) is a morphism over \(k\), and \(h : X' \longrightarrow X\) a morphism over \(S\), such that the following diagram is commutative: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=3em{ X' \ar[r]^-{i'} \ar[d]_{h} & \overline{X}' \ar[d]^{\overline{h}} \\ X \ar[r]_-{i} & \overline{X} } \]
N.B.: we note that it follows from the properness hypotheses that \(\overline{h}^{-1}(i(X)) = i(X')\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma (5.3.2)

For every object \(S\) of \(\mathrm{Sch}_{fs}/k\), the category \(E_S\) is non-empty, possesses non-empty projective limits and finite direct sums which are disjoint and universal.
The fact that the category \(E_S\) is non-empty follows from Chow's lemma.
We shall only indicate the construction of the direct product of two objects \((\overline{X}, X, i)\) and \((\overline{X}', X', i')\) of \(E_S\).

The canonical arrow \(j : X \times_S X' \longrightarrow \overline{X} \times_k \overline{X}'\) is an immersion, and we denote by \(T\) the reduced subscheme of \(\overline{X} \times_k \overline{X}'\) having as underlying space the closure of the image of \(j\): \((T, (X \times_S X')_{\mathrm{red}}, j_{\mathrm{red}})\) satisfies the desired universal property.

(5.3.3) Let \(S\) be an object of \(\mathrm{Sch}_{fs}/k\): we shall say that an object \((\overline{X}, X, i)\) of \(E_S\) satisfies property \(Q\) if \(\overline{X}\) is smooth over \(k\) and if \(i(X)\) is the complement of a normal crossings divisor. We shall say that a morphism \((\overline{h}, h) : (\overline{X}', X', i') \longrightarrow (\overline{X}, X, i)\) satisfies property \(P\) if \(\overline{h}\) is surjective and if \((\overline{X}', X', i')\) satisfies property \(Q\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition (5.3.4)

With the notations of (5.3.3), all the conditions of (5.1.4) are satisfied.
Conditions a), b), d), and c) are easily verified using the resolution of singularities. Moreover, c) is a consequence of f): it thus remains to verify f).

The point is to see that every commutative diagram: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.2em@C=3em{ Z \ar[r]^-{i_Z} \ar[d]_{h} & \overline{Z} \ar[d]^{\overline{h}} \\ X \ar[r]^-{i_X} \ar[d] & \overline{X} \ar[d] \\ S \ar[r] & k \\ S' \ar[u]^{t} & } \] where \((\overline{X}, X, i_X)\) and \((\overline{Z}, Z, i_Z)\) are objects of \(E_S\) with \(\overline{h}\) surjective, can be completed to a commutative diagram: \[ \xymatrix@!0@C=6em@R=4.5em{ & Z' \ar[rr] \ar[dd]|(0.35){h'} \ar[dl]_{i_{Z'}} & & Z \ar[dd]|(0.35){h} \ar[dl]^{i_Z} \\ \overline{Z}' \ar[rr] \ar[dd]_{\overline{h}'} & & \overline{Z} \ar[dd]|(0.65){\overline{h}} & \\ & X' \ar[rr] \ar[dl]_{i_{X'}} & & X \ar[dl]^{i_X} \\ \overline{X}' \ar[rr] & & \overline{X} & } \] (everything over \(S' \xrightarrow{\ t\ } S\) and over \(k\)) where \((\overline{X}', X', i_{X'})\) and \((\overline{Z}', Z', i_{Z'})\) are objects of \(E_{S'}\), with \(\overline{h}'\) surjective. We consider a diagram \[ \xymatrix@R=2.4em@C=2.6em{ T \ar[r]^-{\varphi} \ar[d]_{i_T} & S' \ar[r]^-{t} & S \ar[d] \\ \overline{T} \ar[rr]_-{\psi} & & k } \] where \(\varphi\) is proper and \(\psi\) projective: by base changes, we deduce a diagram: \[ \xymatrix@!0@C=8em@R=4.5em{ & Z \times_S T_{\mathrm{red}} \ar[rr] \ar[dd] \ar[dl]_{p} & & Z \ar[dd] \ar[dl] \\ \overline{Z} \times_k \overline{T}_{\mathrm{red}} \ar[rr] \ar[dd] & & \overline{Z} \ar[dd] & \\ & X \times_S T_{\mathrm{red}} \ar[rr] \ar[dl]_{q} & & X \ar[dl] \\ \overline{X} \times_k \overline{T}_{\mathrm{red}} \ar[rr] & & \overline{X} & } \] (everything over \(T \longrightarrow S' \longrightarrow S\) and over \(\overline{T} \longrightarrow k\)) where \(p\) and \(q\) are immersions; it then suffices to replace \(\overline{Z} \times_k \overline{T}_{\mathrm{red}}\) and \(\overline{X} \times_k \overline{T}_{\mathrm{red}}\) by the closed images of \(p\) and \(q\) to obtain the desired diagram, which completes the proof of (5.3.4).
